cohort: The study included 51 consecutive families whose children were treated for neonatal brachial plexus palsy (NBPP) at the University of Michigan Interdisciplinary Brachial Plexus Program.
finding: The only factor significantly associated with litigation was whether the child had brachial nerve surgery, with 46% of litigating families having surgery compared to 8% of non-litigating families.
mod_finding: There were no differences in litigation rates between operative and spontaneous vaginal births.
